title: RFC: In-Memory Caching and Buffer Eviction Architecture for Event Ingestion

messages.author: sarah_backend_lead
messages.body: As event throughput reaches 85k ops/sec, our hot partition lookups are overwhelming the primary Postgres read-replicas. We need to decide on a standardized in-memory caching tier and eviction policy for the ingestion pipeline before v2.4 ships.

messages.author: raj_infrastructure
messages.body: Proposal A: Let's deploy an external Redis Cluster shared across ingestion workers. It gives us centralized cache invalidation out of the box and simplifies horizontal scaling across worker nodes.

messages.author: elena_perf
messages.body: Benchmarked Proposal A under peak load. The network roundtrip to Redis added 4.2ms to our P99 latency budget (budget is 2ms). During network partition simulations, worker reconnect storms caused buffer bloat. I strongly advise against an external network hop for L1 partition routing.

messages.author: alex_core_dev
messages.body: Proposal B: What about a process-local unbounded in-memory LRU map? Zero network overhead and sub-microsecond access time.

messages.author: sarah_backend_lead
messages.body: A naive LRU map was previously tried in PR #310 and caused Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes during flash crowds when high cardinality keys thrash the working set. It also doesn't handle frequency bias well.

messages.author: elena_perf
messages.body: Proposal C: Two-Tier Hybrid Strategy. Use in-process W-TinyLFU (Window Tiny LFU) bounded cache with a fixed 512MB heap limit per worker for 98% hit rates at sub-millisecond latency. Back it with an optional asynchronous Redis L2 for secondary fallback and cross-process broadcast invalidation.

messages.author: sarah_backend_lead
messages.body: Consensus reached. We will adopt Proposal C (Two-Tier Hybrid Cache with in-process W-TinyLFU L1 and async Redis L2). Proposal A (pure Redis) is rejected due to P99 network latency SLA breaches. Proposal B (unbounded LRU) is rejected due to OOM risk and thrashing. I will document this in ADR-0012 and update ingestion/routing/cache_manager.py.
